Client reports abdominal pain and cloudy dialysis drainage. Fever develops and exit site is mildly tender. Provider evaluates the client and enters time-sensitive orders based on the evolving priority condition. Initial interventions are underway. The nurse reassesses symptoms, vital signs, safety risks, and treatment response. Final reassessment shows mixed response requiring continued clinical judgment and follow-up. Stage 0: Agnes Wright presents with findings concerning for Peritoneal dialysis peritonitis.

debrief.priority_trap: Do not treat peritoneal dialysis peritonitis as routine or benign when progressive cues and abnormal objective data are present.
debrief.safety_lesson: Delayed recognition or unsafe routine care in peritoneal dialysis peritonitis can lead to preventable deterioration.
debrief.outcome_interpretation: Reassessment requires weighing improved and still-concerning findings together.
